messages:
sara (Support): hey team, customer called in — private/VPC deployment behind a customer-managed nginx gateway. they see large spikes of 429s and intermittent 503s when a mobile batch job bursts. asking for quick triage and config suggestions. they say it started after enabling a scheduled churn job.

maria (Customer Infra): thanks, sara. quick details from customer: requests arrive ~2k rps for a ~20s window, then drop. gateway logs show "limit_req: excess" at the same time, upstream (Redwood) returns healthy 200s when not hitting the limiter. they use ingress-nginx controller + Kong in front.

raj (Platform Eng): sounds like gateway-level rate limiting / burst config tripping. can we get a sample request/headers and a small repro? also need to confirm whether the 429 is generated by Kong/nginx vs our runtime. ask them to include the response body for 429s (some gateways include info).

maria (Customer Infra): pasted sample curl they used:

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"large-batch test"}' \
  https://api.customer.example/v1/redwood/generate
```

maria (Customer Infra): gateway log snippet: `2024/10/05 15:12:03 [error] 12345#12345: *98765 limit_req: excess, client: 10.1.2.3, server: ~, request: "POST /v1/redwood/generate HTTP/1.1", host: "api.customer.example"`

oliver (SRE): that is clearly nginx limit_req firing. two quick paths: tune gateway limits (burst/zone) or move to per-API-key token buckets so a single client/user burst doesn't exhaust shared pool. what are their current annotations for ingress-nginx?

maria (Customer Infra): they said they used annotations: `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rps: "100"` and `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-burst: "50"` on the ingress.

raj (Platform Eng): ok that explains it. 100 rps with burst 50 is tiny vs a 2k rps burst. recommended quick mitigation: increase limit and burst to match expected peak, or add a separate ingress for high-throughput jobs. for nginx native config we usually suggest: 

```
# in http context
limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=redwood_zone:50m rate=500r/s;
# per location
limit_req zone=redwood_zone burst=1000 nodelay;
```

raj (Platform Eng): for ingress-nginx annotations, equivalent: `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rps: "500"` and `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-burst: "1000"` (but note some ingress controller versions implement burst differently).

max (Solutions Eng): also recommend switching to a leaky/token bucket per-api-key plugin in Kong so limits track API keys not source IP. Kong rate-limiting plugin config example: `policy=local`, `limit=600`, `burst=800`, `key=consumer` — that keeps heavy tenants from impacting others.

oliver (SRE): also check upstream connection limits and kube/node conntrack. sudden spikes can fill conntrack and cause 502/503. sysctl knobs to check: `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max`, `net.core.somaxconn`, `net.ipv4.tcp_max_syn_backlog`. if conntrack saturates you'll see unrelated timeouts.

maria (Customer Infra): good call — they saw `conntrack: table full` on one node log earlier. they increased nf_conntrack_max and it helped a bit.

sara (Support): customer asked whether Redwood returns any headers we can use to detect throttling vs gateway. what should we ask them to share?

raj (Platform Eng): ask for the raw 429/503 response bodies and headers. gateway 429 usually from nginx/Kong and may include plugin messages. our runtime 429s will include X-Redwood-Request-Id (or similar trace id) and our logs will show `throttled` entry. if they can provide request-id we can correlate on our side. also ask them to enable debug logs on the gateway for a short window: `error_log /var/log/nginx/error.log debug;` to capture the exact limiter decision.

maria (Customer Infra): also worth checking keepalive and proxy settings — nginx defaults can create per-connection head-of-line issues. recommended proxy settings for high throughput: 

```
proxy_http_version 1.1;
proxy_set_header Connection "";
proxy_buffering off;
keepalive_timeout 60;
proxy_connect_timeout 5s;
proxy_read_timeout 60s;
```

max (Solutions Eng): client-side: implement connection reuse and exponential backoff with jitter (we recommend full-jitter). avoid clients opening lots of short-lived connections. sample backoff snippet: `sleep = base * random() * (2 ** attempt)`

oliver (SRE): for kube/ingress specifics: if they use ingress-nginx with a DaemonSet set to hostNetwork=false, ensure `worker-connections` and `worker-processes` are tuned; for nginx ingress we also tune `tcp://` listen backlog via `net.core.somaxconn` and container `ulimit -n`.

maria (Customer Infra): customer asked for a minimal temporary change to test: we've suggested bumping annotations to `limit-rps: "600"` `limit-burst: "1200"` and setting Kong policy to per-consumer. they can roll back after the scheduled job.

raj (Platform Eng): long-term we should advise them to use per-API-key throttles, separate ingress paths for batch vs interactive traffic, and an autoscaling gateway pool. also recommend we provide a short checklist they can paste into their runbook:

- verify where 429 originates (gateway vs runtime) by checking response body + trace id
- tune gateway limit/burst to expected peak for that route
- use per-key token-bucket policy (Kong/Envoy) instead of per-IP if behind NAT/proxies
- increase `nf_conntrack_max` and `somaxconn` on nodes if bursts are connection-heavy
- enable keepalive and connection pooling on clients
- instrument and capture gateway debug logs during repro window

sara (Support): perfect. i'll send those steps and ask them to try the temporary annotation bump + Kong change and get us the 429 responses and any trace ids. i'll loop back here with logs. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deployment "ingress-config-test" started for customer-cfg-42 by maria at 2024-10-05T15:30:12Z

maria (Customer Infra): done for test window. will share logs after the job runs. thanks everyone.

oliver (SRE): if they still see 503s after gateway tuning, ping me and i'll pull runtime traces and look at connection reuse metrics on our side.

sara (Support): closing the loop once we have the post-change logs. cheers.
